parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; with the apostrophe S it gives the possessive
orbs are spheres or balls

explanation.surface: A rather saucy picture of someone gripping a seaman's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: AB is the standard crossword sailor (able-bodied seaman); 'sailor's' supplies AB plus the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in and keep, as a sponge does water, is a synonym for holding.

clue.text: Fungus moved by wind? It is!

parts.note: something moved by the wind was blown, or the wind blew it
it is contracts to it's, written here without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a mushroom was carried off by a gust, and an exclamation confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in IT'S is dropped, as crosswords allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Blewits are edible mushrooms with lilac-tinged caps, so the word names a type of fungus.

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, written as O
to rate someone is an old word for scolding or rebuking them

explanation.surface: Someone who enjoys telling people off and holding forth.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE in the sense of 'scold' is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to speak at length in a pompous or lecturing manner, a direct synonym.

clue.text: City with old railway company first linked to Circle line

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former nationalised UK rail operator
first is written 1st, read as IST
a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A city's history: an old railway firm was first to link up with the Circle line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, a red herring here; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a large port city in south-west England, so it is an example of a city.

indicators.note: a word that embraces another holds it inside itself

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
and is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: A girl hugs a carpenter out on the porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but is the conjunction AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, much like a porch.

clue.text: Birds go initially into rustling trees

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
rustling suggests the leaves stirring, so the letters of trees are stirred around
initially points to the opening letter of the word go

explanation.surface: Birds fly off into trees whose leaves are rustling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rustling' makes ERETS from TREES, and 'into' puts G (the first of 'go', signalled by 'initially') inside after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white herons, a kind of wading bird.

clue.text: A rich man's moved by anti-government argument

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is swayed by a case against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks like 'emotionally touched' but signals rearranging A RICH MANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political doctrine that rejects government altogether, so it is an anti-government philosophy.

clue.text: Lady's maid found showing off in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a servant who helps her mistress get dressed
a kitchen sideboard with open shelves that displays plates and crockery

explanation.surface: A servant is caught preening while in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing off' sounds like vanity, but it describes the furniture displaying china.
explanation.definitionFit: One helps a lady put on her clothes; the other is a cabinet with display shelves for crockery.

clue.text: Sacred belief in control over motor race

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the rest

parts.note: a rein is a strap used to control a horse, and to rein in is to control
motor is a familiar word for a car
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A religious conviction regarding a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motor race' reads as a Grand Prix, but the two words work separately; 'over' places the control piece first in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth of the soul in a new body is a religious doctrine in Hinduism and Buddhism.

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A husband finds time for religious study.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods, so she is a goddess, a divinity.

definitions.meaning: an activity at the start of a meeting that eases tension among strangers
a ship that clears frozen sea lanes so vessels can travel, at sea (the answer to 19)

explanation.surface: A warm-up exercise opens the lines of communication.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is IN THE MAIN, read here as 'at sea', so the second sense is the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a party game that relaxes people and a vessel that cuts paths through frozen waters.

definitions.meaning: to manage or lead, as one leads an orchestra

explanation.definitionFit: Straightforward speaking is frank and candid, and to guide or manage something is to conduct it.

parts.note: to see something is to note it
a patient is a medical case; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look at a patient's wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' as a patient is the doctor's sense: a case on the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old-fashioned term for a wallet that holds banknotes.

clue.text: Remains an outside agent for museum

indicators.note: the two pieces stand outside, one on either side of the next piece

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a mole is a spy or secret agent planted in an organisation

explanation.surface: A spy from outside lingers in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb but is the noun for what is left after burning, and 'outside' wraps the first two words round the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean in Oxford is Britain's oldest public museum, an example of a museum.

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A soldier dines on a fish spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a buffet but is the butter substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people spread on bread.

indicators.note: the first word lies across and outside the next, enclosing it

parts.note: to ford a river is to wade across it
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone wades across to an outlying island's inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: FORD is split around I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiord is a long, narrow arm of the sea between steep cliffs, a type of inlet.

indicators.note: about means going round the next piece

parts.note: sore can mean annoyed or angry
C is short for Conservative, the party of the Tories

explanation.surface: Someone is cross about a Conservative election outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is a nickname for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, hence C.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the result of a game, the tally of points at the end.

indicators.note: seizing something takes it into one's grasp, enclosing it

parts.note: copper is informal for a police officer

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A police officer confiscates a Hungarian chief's weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopper is an axe or cleaver, which can serve as a weapon.

definitions.meaning: the main is an old poetic word for the open ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mostly or generally, and read literally it puts something out on the ocean.

indicators.note: created suggests something newly formed from the name's letters

explanation.surface: A girl named Tabitha built a surrounding world.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where a plant or animal lives.

indicators.note: to ruin something is to wreck it, so the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A walker went past a ruin standing on a ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' looks like a noun for an old building but works as the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To be passed by is to be overlooked or disregarded, which is the sense here.

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: based means located or stationed somewhere

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, upper-case letter

explanation.surface: A partisan fighter is stationed outside the Indian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian capital' suggests Delhi but gives only I.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan person favours one side, so is prejudiced or one-sided.

indicators.note: about means wrapping round the next piece

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist, mainly on England's east coast
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person worries about a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like the verb 'worry' but is the noun for a coastal mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with strict views on morality who lectures others about it.

parts.note: BA is British Airways
tons means lots, a great quantity

explanation.surface: An airline owns a large number of golf or night clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs or golf, but means sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Batons are short sticks such as police truncheons, which are clubs.

indicators.note: the name shows the letters that sit inside it, spanning the two names

explanation.surface: A woman called Anita Stewart reveals her prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discrimination' suggests prejudice but means discernment.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrimination here is fine judgment in aesthetic matters, as in having good judgment in art.

parts.note: spoils are plunder or loot taken in war
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A wet blanket keeps the stolen goods left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like 'left behind', but it is the nautical side, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins others' fun, which is exactly what a killjoy does.

clue.text: Small boat found in the Channel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A little boat is discovered in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small island lying in the English Channel, so it is a place there.

indicators.note: kidnapping means taking and holding someone inside

parts.note: fiends are devils or demons
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: Witches' spirits and demons abduct a red-haired person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiars' suggests witches' spirits, fitting the demons, but here means close acquaintances.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiars are close acquaintances, people one knows well, hence pals.

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car
to tend is to look after or care for

explanation.surface: A fashion model looks after her escorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' gives T from the Model T Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone someone is to accompany them, so going along with them is a synonym.
